statement: The Linear Kalman Filter recursively computes the Gaussian belief distribution $\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t}, \mathbf{P}_{t|t})$ in two steps (note: the source writes $\mathbf{R}_t$ for process noise covariance and $\mathbf{Q}_t$ for measurement noise covariance; here we rename them consistently to $\mathbf{Q}_t$ for process noise covariance and $\mathbf{R}_t$ for measurement noise covariance). Prediction step: $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1} = \mathbf{F}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1} + \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t$ and $\mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} = \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{P}_{t-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{Q}_t$. Update step: $\mathbf{K}_t = \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} (\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{R}_t)^{-1}$, $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1} + \mathbf{K}_t (\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{H}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1})$, and $\mathbf{P}_{t|t} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_t \mathbf{H}_t) \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}$.

steps.text:
Express the predicted belief $\overline{\text{bel}}(\mathbf{x}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}, \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1})$ as the marginalization integral over $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$ of the Gaussian state transition distribution $p(\mathbf{x}_t \mid \mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{x}_{t-1} + \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t, \mathbf{Q}_t)$ and the prior belief $\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}) \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1}, \mathbf{P}_{t-1})$:
$$\overline{\text{bel}}(\mathbf{x}_t) = \int p(\mathbf{x}_t \mid \mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t)\,\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1})\,d\mathbf{x}_{t-1} = \eta \int \exp(-\mathbf{L}_t)\,d\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$$
where
$$\mathbf{L}_t = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t)^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t) + \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1})^{\intercal} \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1})$$

Decompose the quadratic exponent $\mathbf{L}_t$ into a term $\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t)$ containing all dependence on $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$ and a term $\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t)$ independent of $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$, factoring $\exp(-\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t))$ out of the integral:
$$\overline{\text{bel}}(\mathbf{x}_t) = \eta \exp(-\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t)) \int \exp(-\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t))\,d\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$$

To isolate the $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$ dependence in $\mathbf{L}_t$, take the first and second partial derivatives of $\mathbf{L}_t$ with respect to $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$:
$$\frac{\partial \mathbf{L}_t}{\partial \mathbf{x}_{t-1}} = -\mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t) + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1})$$
$$\frac{\partial^2 \mathbf{L}_t}{\partial \mathbf{x}_{t-1}^2} = \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1} := \Psi_t^{-1}$$
Setting $\frac{\partial \mathbf{L}_t}{\partial \mathbf{x}_{t-1}} = 0$ and solving for $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$ gives the mean of $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$:
$$\mathbf{x}_{t-1} = \Psi_t \left[ \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t) + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1} \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1} \right]$$

Complete the square in $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$ to write $\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t)$ as a quadratic form with inverse covariance $\Psi_t^{-1}$:
$$\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \Psi_t[\mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1}(\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t) + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1}]\right)^{\intercal} \Psi_t^{-1} \left(\mathbf{x}_{t-1} - \Psi_t[\mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1}(\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t) + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1}]\right)$$
Because $\det(2\pi \Psi_t)^{-1/2} \exp(-\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t))$ is a normalized Gaussian density over $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$, its integral over $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$ equals $1$, so $\int \exp(-\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t))\,d\mathbf{x}_{t-1} = \det(2\pi \Psi_t)^{1/2}$ is constant with respect to $\mathbf{x}_t$, yielding:
$$\overline{\text{bel}}(\mathbf{x}_t) = \eta' \exp(-\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t))$$

Compute $\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t) = \mathbf{L}_t - \mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t)$ by expanding the quadratic forms and cancelling all quadratic and linear terms in $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$:
$$\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t) = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t)^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t) + \frac{1}{2}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1}^{\intercal} \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1} \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1} - \frac{1}{2}[\mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1}(\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t) + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1}]^{\intercal} (\mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1})^{-1} [\mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1}(\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t) + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1}]$$

Take the first derivative of $\mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t)$ with respect to $\mathbf{x}_t$ and apply the matrix inversion lemma to simplify $\mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} - \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t (\mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1})^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} = (\mathbf{Q}_t + \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{P}_{t-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal})^{-1}$:
$$\frac{\partial \mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t)}{\partial \mathbf{x}_t} = (\mathbf{Q}_t + \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{P}_{t-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal})^{-1}(\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t) - \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t (\mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1})^{-1} \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1} \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1}$$

Set $\frac{\partial \mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t)}{\partial \mathbf{x}_t} = 0$ to find the predicted mean $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}$, and take the second derivative $\frac{\partial^2 \mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t)}{\partial \mathbf{x}_t^2}$ to find the inverse predicted covariance $\mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}^{-1}$:
$$\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1} = \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t + (\mathbf{Q}_t + \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{P}_{t-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal}) \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t (\mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t + \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1})^{-1} \mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1} \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1} = \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t + \mathbf{F}_t (\mathbf{I} + \mathbf{P}_{t-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t)(\mathbf{P}_{t-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{Q}_t^{-1} \mathbf{F}_t + \mathbf{I})^{-1} \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1} = \mathbf{F}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t-1} + \mathbf{B}_t \mathbf{u}_t$$
$$\frac{\partial^2 \mathbf{L}_t(\mathbf{x}_t)}{\partial \mathbf{x}_t^2} = (\mathbf{Q}_t + \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{P}_{t-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal})^{-1} \implies \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} = \mathbf{F}_t \mathbf{P}_{t-1} \mathbf{F}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{Q}_t$$

For the update step, express the posterior belief $\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t}, \mathbf{P}_{t|t})$ via Bayes' rule as the normalized product of the measurement likelihood $p(\mathbf{z}_t \mid \mathbf{x}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{x}_t, \mathbf{R}_t)$ and the prior belief $\overline{\text{bel}}(\mathbf{x}_t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}, \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1})$:
$$\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_t) = \eta\,p(\mathbf{z}_t \mid \mathbf{x}_t)\,\overline{\text{bel}}(\mathbf{x}_t) = \eta \exp(-\mathbf{J}_t)$$
where
$$\mathbf{J}_t = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{x}_t)^{\intercal} \mathbf{R}_t^{-1} (\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{x}_t) + \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{x}_t - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1})^{\intercal} \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_t - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1})$$

Take the first and second partial derivatives of $\mathbf{J}_t$ with respect to $\mathbf{x}_t$ to identify the inverse posterior covariance $\mathbf{P}_{t|t}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{\partial \mathbf{J}_t}{\partial \mathbf{x}_t} = -\mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{R}_t^{-1} (\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{x}_t) + \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_t - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1})$$
$$\frac{\partial^2 \mathbf{J}_t}{\partial \mathbf{x}_t^2} = \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{R}_t^{-1} \mathbf{H}_t + \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}^{-1} := \mathbf{P}_{t|t}^{-1}$$

Set $\frac{\partial \mathbf{J}_t}{\partial \mathbf{x}_t} = 0$, add and subtract $\mathbf{H}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}$ inside the measurement residual, and solve for the posterior mean $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t}$:
$$\mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{R}_t^{-1} (\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{x}_t + \mathbf{H}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1} - \mathbf{H}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}) = \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_t - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1})$$
$$\mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{R}_t^{-1} (\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{H}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}) = (\mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{R}_t^{-1} \mathbf{H}_t + \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}^{-1})(\mathbf{x}_t - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1}) = \mathbf{P}_{t|t}^{-1} (\mathbf{x}_t - \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1})$$
Defining the Kalman gain $\mathbf{K}_t = \mathbf{P}_{t|t} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{R}_t^{-1}$ gives:
$$\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1} + \mathbf{K}_t (\mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{H}_t \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t|t-1})$$

Apply the matrix inversion lemma to $\mathbf{P}_{t|t} = (\mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}^{-1} + \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{R}_t^{-1} \mathbf{H}_t)^{-1}$ and rewrite the Kalman gain $\mathbf{K}_t$ in terms of the prior covariance $\mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}$:
$$\mathbf{K}_t = \mathbf{P}_{t|t} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{R}_t^{-1} (\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{R}_t)(\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{R}_t)^{-1} = \mathbf{P}_{t|t} (\mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} \mathbf{R}_t^{-1} \mathbf{H}_t + \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}^{-1}) \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} (\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{R}_t)^{-1} = \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} (\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{R}_t)^{-1}$$
Substituting this into the matrix inversion lemma expansion yields the updated covariance:
$$\mathbf{P}_{t|t} = \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} - \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} (\mathbf{R}_t + \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal})^{-1} \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} = \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} - \mathbf{K}_t \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_t \mathbf{H}_t) \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}$$

assumptions.assumption: The state transition $p(\mathbf{x}_t \mid \mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \mathbf{u}_t)$, measurement likelihood $p(\mathbf{z}_t \mid \mathbf{x}_t)$, and prior belief $\text{bel}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1})$ are linear-Gaussian.
assumptions.breaks_when: The transition or observation models are nonlinear or the noise/prior distributions are non-Gaussian, preventing exact quadratic expansion in the exponent.

assumptions.assumption: Covariance matrices $\mathbf{Q}_t$, $\mathbf{R}_t$, $\mathbf{P}_{t-1}$, $\mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}$, and intermediate curvature matrices $\Psi_t^{-1}$ and $\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{R}_t$ are positive definite (invertible).
assumptions.breaks_when: Noise or state error covariances are singular (e.g., deterministic transitions with $\mathbf{Q}_t = 0$ in the information form $\mathbf{Q}_t^{-1}$, or noiseless measurements with $\mathbf{R}_t = 0$).

failure_modes.signature: Matrix inverse $\mathbf{Q}_t^{-1}$, $\mathbf{R}_t^{-1}$, $\mathbf{P}_{t-1}^{-1}$, or innovation covariance inverse $(\mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_{t|t-1} \mathbf{H}_t^{\intercal} + \mathbf{R}_t)^{-1}$ does not exist.
failure_modes.cause: Zero process noise, zero measurement noise, or loss of positive definiteness in $\mathbf{P}_{t|t} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_t \mathbf{H}_t)\mathbf{P}_{t|t-1}$.

instantiation.why_here: The project does not implement a Linear Kalman Filter directly; instead, the `ekf_local` and `ekf_global` nodes use `robot_localization` (`src/ekf.cpp`), which implements the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) built on the two-step Kalman prediction and update recursion over a 15-entry state vector. In `src/ekf.cpp:436`, the prediction covariance update propagates `estimate_error_covariance_` via `transfer_function_jacobian_ * estimate_error_covariance_ * transfer_function_jacobian_.transpose()` and adds `delta_sec * (*process_noise_covariance)`. The two nodes fuse measurements from `/odom_cov` (`odom_cov_relay`), `/imu` (`parameter_bridge`), `/odometry/gps` (`navsat_transform`), and `/rtk/heading` (`rtk_sim`).

concrete.in_your_project: The 15x1 state vector tracked by `ekf_local` and `ekf_global` containing X, Y, Z, Roll, Pitch, Yaw, Vx, Vy, Vz, Vroll, Vpitch, Vyaw, Ax, Ay, and Az.
`estimate_error_covariance_` (15x15) on the right-hand side of `src/ekf.cpp:436` before the prediction step, initialized by the 15x15 `initial_estimate_covariance` parameter.
`estimate_error_covariance_` (15x15) after multiplying by `transfer_function_jacobian_` and its transpose and adding `delta_sec * (*process_noise_covariance)` in `src/ekf.cpp:436`.
`transfer_function_jacobian_` (15x15) in `src/ekf.cpp:436`, which pre-multiplies `estimate_error_covariance_` and post-multiplies it via `.transpose()`.
`delta_sec * (*process_noise_covariance)` (15x15) in `src/ekf.cpp:436`, where `process_noise_covariance` is a 15x15 diagonal matrix configured in `ekf_local.yaml` and `ekf_global.yaml`.

The measurement vectors read from `/odom_cov` (`odom0`, fusing Vx, Vy, Vyaw), `/odometry/gps` (`odom1` in `ekf_global`, fusing X, Y), `/imu` (`imu0`, fusing Vyaw), and `/rtk/heading` (`imu1` in `ekf_global`, fusing Yaw).
The observation submatrix rows selected from the 15 state entries by `odom0_config` (Vx, Vy, Vyaw), `odom1_config` (X, Y), `imu0_config` (Vyaw), and `imu1_config` (Yaw).

The measurement noise covariance matrices attached to incoming messages: in `src/agrios_control/agrios_control/odom_cov_relay.py:12-16`, `msg.twist.covariance` (6x6, 36 entries) sets `c[0] = 0.05` (vx), `c[7] = 0.05` (vy), and `c[35] = 0.02` (vyaw) with all other entries `0.0`; in `src/agrios_control/agrios_control/rtk_sim.py:79-105`, `hdg.orientation_covariance` and `fix.position_covariance` (with `COVARIANCE_TYPE_DIAGONAL_KNOWN`) are set on the messages while `hdg.angular_velocity_covariance[0]` and `hdg.linear_acceleration_covariance[0]` are set to `-1.0`.

instantiation.notation: The sheet denotes the state error covariance as \mathbf{P}, the state transition matrix as \mathbf{F}_t, and the process noise covariance as \mathbf{Q}_t (noting the underlying textbook source reverses \mathbf{Q}_t and \mathbf{R}_t), whereas `src/ekf.cpp:436` names them `estimate_error_covariance_`, `transfer_function_jacobian_`, and `process_noise_covariance` (scaled by `delta_sec`).
